title: Study-conditioned candidate annotations of context-residualized family-mass directions
caption_markdown_lines: **Figure 3 | Study-conditioned candidate annotations of context-residualized family-mass directions.** A local SVD mode is a dataset-specific latent direction; local modes are assigned to parent families F1–F16. For perturbation *i* and family *f*, the source quantity is normalized absolute family mass, `A_if = [Σ_(m∈f) |U_im S_m|] / [Σ_g Σ_(m∈g) |U_im S_m|]`, and the downstream coordinate is its context residual, `R_if = A_if − mean_c(i)(A_f)`, averaged across occurrences of the same gene. Thus `A_if ≥ 0`, and family masses sum to one before residualization. “Lower” and “upper” denote below- and above-context-mean residual mass, respectively; they do not denote intrinsic negative or positive biology. Absolute mode scores remove the arbitrary polarity of an SVD vector. A candidate functional annotation is a manually curated shorthand applied after testing and consolidating one or more family/query views; it is not the identity of a latent mode, a mechanism, or a constraint law.

**a, Operational definition and corrected workflow.** Four legacy query views—lower, upper, largest absolute residual, and high-confidence largest absolute residual—were attempted for each of 14 nonempty parent families, giving 56 original views. Explicit sign filtering removed the invalid F1, F3, and F15 upper views, leaving 53 corrected valid views. Lower/upper queries targeted 30 genes and absolute-residual queries targeted 40 genes, but all genes tied at a boundary were retained; corrected realized query sizes therefore range from 20 to 362. Each view was tested against 3,807 de-duplicated MSigDB v2026.1.Hs gene sets from Hallmark, Reactome, Gene Ontology biological process, cellular component and molecular function, and KEGG. One-sided Fisher over-representation analysis (ORA) used the selected tail. The one-sided Mann–Whitney rank analysis used all eligible gene scores: `R` for upper, `−R` for lower, and `|R|` for absolute-residual views. The pooled background contains 1,229 genes; high-confidence absolute views instead use their eligible 255-gene universe for both ORA and rank analysis. Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment was performed separately for ORA and rank across all 201,771 corrected view–term tests per method. Analytic term candidates required ORA `q ≤ 0.05`, overlap of at least 3 and odds ratio of at least 2, or rank `q ≤ 0.05` and mean-score difference of at least 0.05. Terms were consolidated at Jaccard similarity 0.70 before manual, post hoc axis naming, representative-term choice, and failure-mode review. Displayed terms are illustrative rather than exhaustive.

The resulting registry contains 15 collapsed candidate groups: 3 headline, 6 supporting, 4 exploratory, and 2 excluded or unresolved. **b,** The matrix displays the nine manually curated headline or supporting annotations. Companion Supplementary Figure 3 expands the same six supporting annotations; it does not provide six additional independent candidates. Matrix entries are descriptive maxima over each label’s constituent family/query views: corrected ORA and rank `−log10(q)`, maximum absolute full-data RidgeCV coefficient `|β|`, maximum absolute high-confidence Spearman association `|ρ|`, and maximum dominant-study proxy share. `NR` denotes no retained result, not a numerical zero. Printed values are the underlying summaries; cell shade is normalized within each column only and neither makes unlike metrics commensurate nor defines a combined evidence score. ORA and rank reuse the same coordinates and overlapping gene-set memberships. Ridge and Spearman summaries reuse the same endpoint, `essentiality_strength = −mean DepMap GeneEffect`, and therefore are also dependent rather than independent replications.

**c, Shared-endpoint fitness summaries.** Signed family-level estimates are aligned by parent-family row. Ridge predictors were standardized but the response was not; each `β` is therefore in essentiality-strength units per one-standard-deviation predictor within the full 16-feature regularized coding (1,229 genes; RidgeCV `α = 31.6228`). Spearman `ρ(|R|)` is the association between absolute residual magnitude and the same essentiality-strength endpoint among high-confidence genes with a nonzero family coordinate; family-specific `n` ranges from 57 to 227. Neither estimate has an uncertainty interval. The 16 residual features are closed and have matrix rank 12; F15 is `0.19354839 × F3`, F6 is `−F5`, and F4 and F13 are zero. Accordingly, the ridge coefficients are coding- and penalty-dependent descriptive estimates, not independently identifiable family effects.

**d, Study-conditioned F14 cytokine coherence.** Tie-inclusive correction yields 41 genes in the F14 lower-residual query, tested against the pooled 1,229-gene universe. Representative, manually selected ORA terms are cytokine activity (`q = 1.98 × 10^−55`, odds ratio 2,188.6, 37/41 genes), cytokine–receptor interaction (`9.90 × 10^−40`, 321.4, 32/41), cytokine receptor binding (`1.40 × 10^−31`, 132.3, 30/41), interleukin signalling (`4.07 × 10^−27`, 71.3, 33/41), and JAK–STAT signalling (`3.75 × 10^−25`, 96.1, 25/41). All 41 query genes have the CuiHacohen2023 study proxy. These results therefore describe study-conditioned pathway coherence rather than a general F14 cytokine axis.

**e, Deduplicated F3/F15 chromatin coherence.** F3 and F15 are scaled copies rather than independent discoveries: `F15 = 0.19354839 × F3`. The high-confidence largest-`|R|` query contains 40 genes and is evaluated in the corrected 255-gene eligible universe. Representative ORA terms are chromatin organization (`q = 3.52 × 10^−15`, odds ratio 55.2, 26/40 genes), epigenetic regulation (`1.67 × 10^−8`, 20.5, 20/40), histone methyltransferase activity (`7.26 × 10^−8`, infinite odds ratio, 12/40), histone lysine methylation (`7.26 × 10^−8`, infinite odds ratio, 12/40), and histone-modifying activity (`1.12 × 10^−7`, 28.0, 16/40). Thirty-five of the 40 genes (87.5%) have a LaraAstiasoHuntly2023 study proxy. The displayed `q` values use the corrected high-confidence universe; they do not establish independent-study replication.

**f, Required failure modes and falsifiers.** The original dedicated F12 translation/RQC enrichment panel is replaced because its absolute-residual query (40/40 genes) and lower-residual query (30/30 genes) are entirely concentrated in ReplogleWeissman2022 K562. The panel also records the F14 study concentration, the F3/F15 duplication and LaraAstiasoHuntly2023 concentration, and the non-identifiability of ridge coefficients under the closed, rank-deficient feature coding. General candidate-axis claims require leave-study-out reconstruction, study-matched nulls, independent-study recurrence, a declared contrast basis, and study-block bootstrap uncertainty. Panels d and e are representative evidence views, and panel f is a robustness boundary; none is an independent replication of another panel. Overall, the figure supports study-conditioned pathway coherence in manually curated, pipeline-dependent summaries. It does not identify validated biological programs, universal axes, mechanisms, or causal constraint laws.
alt: Six-panel Figure 3 defines above- and below-context residual family-mass queries, summarizes nine manually curated candidate annotations, shows two dependent GeneEffect association measures, presents study-conditioned F14 cytokine and deduplicated F3/F15 chromatin enrichment, and documents study concentration and compositional non-identifiability. The evidence is associative and pipeline-dependent, not proof of general biological axes.
accessible_description_markdown_lines: The figure is a two-column, three-row composition on a white background. Teal marks headline annotations, grey marks supporting annotations, blue and purple distinguish the two fitness summaries, orange marks the F14 cytokine result, purple marks the deduplicated chromatin result, and red-brown warning elements identify limitations. Color never supplies the only distinction: every row, estimate, term, query size, and warning is directly labelled.
### Panel a — Operational definition and audit workflow

Six connected boxes define the analysis. First, absolute SVD-score mass is summed within each parent family and normalized across families within a perturbation profile, producing non-negative values that sum to one. Second, the context-specific family mean is subtracted; residuals can lie below or above zero. Because the source mass uses absolute SVD-mode scores, the residual sign is not an SVD pole: “lower” means below the assigned-context expectation and “upper” means above it.

The legacy analysis attempted four views for each of 14 nonempty parent families, or 56 views. Corrected explicit sign filtering removes `F1_pos`, `F3_pos`, and `F15_pos`, leaving 53 valid views. Boundary ties are all retained, so target sizes of 30 genes for lower/upper tails and 40 for absolute tails produce realized sizes from 20 to 362. ORA and rank analysis test 3,807 de-duplicated gene sets. Fisher ORA compares the selected query with the eligible background. The one-sided Mann–Whitney analysis compares the coordinate-derived score in each gene set with the score outside it. The pooled background has 1,229 genes; high-confidence absolute views use 255 eligible genes. Separate global Benjamini–Hochberg corrections cover 201,771 tests for each method. Candidate rows satisfy the stated `q` and effect/overlap filters, after which 0.70-Jaccard consolidation, axis naming, representative-term selection, and failure-mode review are manual and post hoc. The 15 collapsed groups comprise 3 headline, 6 supporting, 4 exploratory, and 2 excluded or unresolved groups. The main figure orders and displays all 9 headline/supporting groups; Supplementary Figure 3 expands the same 6 supporting groups. The enrichment-term order in panels d and e is a curated display order, not a ranking over all 3,807 tested sets.
### Panel b — Nine manually curated annotations

Nine rows are arranged as three headline rows followed by six supporting rows. The first two numerical columns are corrected ORA and rank `−log10(q)`; the next two are the maximum absolute RidgeCV coefficient and maximum absolute high-confidence Spearman correlation with mean DepMap essentiality strength; the last is the largest fraction of a query carrying one dominant study proxy. The numeric cell values are:
| Tier | Candidate shorthand | Generating view(s) | ORA −log10(q) | Rank −log10(q) | Max abs(β) | Max abs(ρ) | Max study share |
| Headline | Cytokine / JAK–STAT | F14 lower | 54.7 | 16.0 | 0.023 | 0.291 | 100% |
| Headline | Chromatin / epigenetic | F3/F15 high-confidence absolute | 14.5 | NR | 0.029 | 0.020 | 87.5% |
| Headline | Translation / RQC | F12 lower and absolute | 9.9 | 21.1 | 0.249 | 0.156 | 100% |
| Supporting | Chromatin–cytokine | F10 high-confidence absolute, absolute, and upper | 39.0 | 21.5 | 0.035 | 0.135 | 100% |
| Supporting | OXPHOS / TCA | F7 upper | 8.9 | 11.1 | 0.101 | 0.441 | 100% |
| Supporting | Lysosome / ECM | F10 lower | 5.3 | 4.3 | 0.035 | 0.135 | 100% |
| Supporting | rRNA biogenesis | F11 lower and absolute | 4.3 | 3.3 | 0.039 | 0.032 | 100% |
| Supporting | SREBP / cholesterol | F5 lower and F6 upper | 6.1 | 5.1 | 0.037 | 0.044 | 100% |
| Supporting | Antigen-receptor / tolerance | F1 absolute and lower | 3.1 | 3.6 | 0.028 | 0.037 | 64.3% |

`NR` means that no result passed the retained-result criteria; it is not a zero-valued effect. Each shade is scaled only within its own column. The annotations are manual biological shorthands, not measured quantities. ORA and rank are dependent summaries of overlapping inputs, and the two fitness columns share one endpoint.
### Panel c — Shared-endpoint fitness summaries

Eight parent-family rows each show a blue circular RidgeCV coefficient and a purple square Spearman `ρ(|R|)` on separate signed horizontal tracks with zero reference lines; values are printed directly. `essentiality_strength = −mean DepMap GeneEffect`, so larger values indicate stronger mean essentiality. Ridge coefficients use 1,229 genes and standardized predictors; they are in endpoint units per one-standard-deviation predictor. Correlations use only nonzero coordinates among the 255 high-confidence genes, yielding family-specific samples:
| Parent-family row | Ridge β | Spearman ρ(abs residual) | ρ sample size | Structural note |
| F3/F15 chromatin / epigenetic | +0.029 for each | −0.020 for each | 90 | F15 = 0.19354839 × F3 |
| F10 mixed chromatin–cytokine / lysosome | +0.035 | −0.135 | 95 | One parent family supplies two curated labels |
| F5/F6 SREBP / cholesterol | −0.037 for F5; +0.037 for F6 | −0.044 for each | 57 | F6 = −F5 |
| F1 antigen-receptor / tolerance | −0.028 | +0.037 | 113 | — |

No uncertainty intervals are available. Both tracks use the same essentiality-strength endpoint and overlapping genes, so their agreement or disagreement is descriptive rather than independent validation. Closure and exact linear dependencies make individual ridge coefficients sensitive to coding and penalty choice.
### Panel d — Study-conditioned cytokine coherence

An orange lollipop plot shows five manually selected representative ORA terms for the tie-inclusive F14 lower-residual query. Horizontal position is `−log10(q)`. The right-hand columns print the corrected global `q`, odds ratio, and overlap over the 41-gene query:
| Representative term | q | Odds ratio | Overlap/query |
| Cytokine–receptor interaction | 9.90 × 10^−40 | 321.4 | 32/41 |
| Cytokine receptor binding | 1.40 × 10^−31 | 132.3 | 30/41 |
| Interleukin signalling | 4.07 × 10^−27 | 71.3 | 33/41 |

The background is the 1,229-gene pooled atlas. All 41 query genes have the CuiHacohen2023 study proxy. The enrichment is therefore labelled study-conditioned; the panel does not establish a transportable F14 biological axis.
### Panel e — Deduplicated chromatin coherence

A purple lollipop plot shows five manually selected representative ORA terms for the F3/F15 high-confidence largest-absolute-residual query. `F15 = 0.19354839 × F3`, so the panel treats them as one candidate rather than two replications. The query contains 40 genes and the eligible background contains 255:
| Representative term | q | Odds ratio | Overlap/query |
| Chromatin organization | 3.52 × 10^−15 | 55.2 | 26/40 |
| Epigenetic regulation | 1.67 × 10^−8 | 20.5 | 20/40 |
| Histone methyltransferase activity | 7.26 × 10^−8 | ∞ | 12/40 |
| Histone lysine methylation | 7.26 × 10^−8 | ∞ | 12/40 |
| Histone-modifying activity | 1.12 × 10^−7 | 28.0 | 16/40 |

The infinite odds ratios arise from empty comparison cells, not infinite biological effects. Thirty-five query genes, or 87.5%, have a LaraAstiasoHuntly2023 study proxy. The corrected `q` values use the 255-gene high-confidence universe, but no leave-study-out reconstruction is available.
### Panel f — Why the candidates are not general biological axes
Four warning rows make the main robustness failures explicit:
1. The tie-inclusive F14 lower query has 41 genes, all with the CuiHacohen2023 study proxy; the cytokine result requires leave-CuiHacohen2023-out reconstruction and a study-matched null.

2. `F15 = 0.19354839 × F3`, and 87.5% of the 40 high-confidence query genes have a LaraAstiasoHuntly2023 study proxy; this is one study-concentrated chromatin candidate, not two independent replications.

3. The F12 absolute query is 40/40 and the F12 lower query is 30/30 ReplogleWeissman2022 K562; the translation/RQC annotation requires leave-study-out reconstruction and independent-study recurrence. This failure mode replaces the original dedicated F12 enrichment panel.

4. The 16 closed family features have matrix rank 12, F6 is the sign reverse of F5, and F4 and F13 are zero; ridge coefficients require a declared contrast basis and study-block bootstrap before family-specific interpretation.

The bottom banner lists the minimum next analyses: leave-study-out rebuilds, matched nulls, and a contrast-basis bootstrap. Across all panels, enrichment `q` values, association summaries, and curated labels are associative and pipeline-dependent. The figure supports descriptive, study-conditioned pathway coherence only; it does not demonstrate a validated pathway, general biological program, mechanism, universal constraint, or causal law.
responsive_presentation_requirement: The full 2,400-pixel web image, 1,200-pixel view, publication PNG, PDF, and SVG are intended reading surfaces. The audited 480-pixel-wide composite is structurally intact and collision-free, but its fine text is zoom-dependent and is not comfortably readable at native 480-pixel display size. The website must preserve an uncropped overview and provide a keyboard- and touch-accessible way to open or zoom the full-resolution PNG or SVG. Do not claim native 480-pixel legibility, and do not replace the approved composite with an unverified mobile crop.
